title: COP31: Climate deal 'not adopted,' summit president says
summary: The summit was extended as nations worked to reach a deal, but they couldn't agree on including fossil fuels. European nations, small island states and activists have criticized oil-producing…
byline: Jenipher Camino Gonzalez, Emmy Sasipornkarn, Nik Martin, Dmytro Hubenko, Patrick Große, Mark Hallam, Karl Sexton

image.caption: Despite weeks of talks and an extension, a deal has remain elusiveImage: Khalil Hamra/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: COP31 fails to agree climate deal amid fossil fuel rift

blocks.caption: Weeks of tense negotiations have failed to yield a dealImage: Murad Sezer/REUTERS

blocks.text: The COP31 climate summit has failed to agree on a final joint declaration.
During a plenary session, the summit's Turkish president acknowledged there would be no climate deal.

"I understand that there is no agreement on this text. For that reason, these decisions have not been adopted," Murat Kurum, who is also Turkey's environment minister, told a closing plenary in the Mediterranean city of Antalya.

The rift centered on whether to include the phaseout of fossil fuels in the final declaration. Scientists say the burning of fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas is the main cause of global warming.
European nations, smaller island states and climate activists have criticized oil-producing countries for the omission.
